Starting a business in Cyprus, from the barest registration to a café

What it takes, in steps, fees and published times, to trade in Cyprus in one's own name, as a company, online and with premises; what each step up gives in return; how businesses opened in 2022–2026 went through it; whom to hire for which step and what firms publish as their prices; what changes when the owner is foreign; why the rules moved and what is coming.

Reference study, not legal or tax advice. Every statement carries its status as of 6 October 2026 and a number that leads to the memory record behind it and to the document that record was read in. Prices are firms' own published prices on the dates given, not a tariff; times are published times, not commitments; nothing is added up into a total. The last section lists what was not established and when to look again.

gid research round cyprus-setup-guide · 6 October 2026 · 472 records stored in three waves, 79.7% read in the primary document · sixteen research slices, each checked by two adversarial verifiers: 277 of 385 researcher facts corrected, 4 refuted · written from the records by seven writers and checked item by item by seven checkers, who corrected 198 of 548 items

  1. Question 1Four rungs: each adds filings, and only the company limits every member's liabilityAs of 6 October 2026 a person may trade with no Registrar filing; a business name adds €10 and €80 and no yearly return; a partnership €120; a company an advocate, a €165 filing, a yearly return and audit or review. In return the company limits members' liability, within statutory exceptions, and a working shareholder is insured as an employed person.
  2. Path 1Path 1: Social Insurance and a tax number; the Registrar only for a trade nameA self-employed person registers with the Social Insurance Services by the day work starts and enters the Tax Register; a trade name adds name approval and form EE1 (€10 and €80). No step found is reserved to an advocate. An EU citizen may start before his registration certificate; a third-country national first needs a status that allows it.
  3. Path 2A private company: advocate-drafted papers and HE1 at the Registrar, then tax, owners, VAT, staffFormed at the Registrar after name approval, on a memorandum and articles only an advocate may draft; the Registrar's HE1 is an advocate's oath, though the Law also allows a director or secretary. Tax registration via CY Login (within 60 days), beneficial owners (90 days) and VAT when due follow. As of 6 October 2026 no authority publishes processing times.
  4. Path 3Selling online to consumers: no licence aimed at it, but site duties, VAT and producer dutiesNo licence is aimed at selling online. A web shop adds information and withdrawal duties to consumers, product-safety details on each offer, VAT for sales into other EU states (the One Stop Shop only after Cyprus VAT registration) and, where the shop itself imports or first supplies the goods, producer, customs or cosmetics steps.
  5. Path 4A shop needs a municipal licence; a café adds tourism and health approvals and missing use permitsIn a municipality a shop needs the s. 56 premises licence (deemed granted after four months' silence on complete papers) and pays a yearly trade fee. A café also needs permits for catering use where the premises lacks them, a sanitary certificate, an approved manager and the Deputy Ministry of Tourism licence; alcohol and sound are licensed apart.
  6. Question 2Real cases 2022-2026: register and web dates are public; no licence issue date was foundRead from the Registrar's free search, web archives, the press and the tourism lists as of 6 October 2026. Two of the barest businesses were public before their registration; the tourism lists seen print at most a licence's expiry, no issue date; B-READY 2025's 11.5 days for company entry is an expert median, not a case.
  7. Question 3Only an advocate may draft a company's founding documents; later routine filings name no lawyerCyprus law reserves drafting a company's memorandum and articles to a practising advocate, audits to licensed auditors, plans to registered engineers and architects, and director, secretary and office services offered to others to eligible persons. Firms publish formation prices on different bases as of 6 October 2026; none is an official fee.
  8. The foreign elementA foreign founder files the same company forms; permits, papers, screening and banks add the restThe Registrar's criteria identify founders by passport or identity number and ask for no residence permit; per an agency report, she seeks other services' views on companies with Turkish or Turkish Cypriot officers. The foreign element shows mainly in the right to run a business, papers from abroad, branches, screening, land, sanctions and banks.
  9. WhyWhy rules changed: reasons sit in bills, committee reports and speeches; some changes state noneStated reasons come from Government reports to the House, MPs' memoranda, committee reports, a Minister's speech and the Fiscal Council; press accounts fill gaps. The 15% corporate rate has two accounts. The 2026 strike-off drive, the 2018 shell-company circular and the minimum-wage decree state no reason.
  10. What is comingWhat is coming: Cyprus bills mostly undated, EU dates fixed, several transpositions lateAs of 6 October 2026 the Cyprus changes that touch a founder are bills, drafts or plans, and few have a dated next step. EU acts set fixed dates; for consumer credit, the single permit, pay transparency and beneficial-owner register access the Cyprus deadline had passed with no law found. Nothing here is in force unless a row says so.
  11. CalendarCalendar to 2028: fixed deadlines of adopted acts and meetings where change may be announcedEach entry says whether it is a date set by an adopted act, a meeting at which something may be announced, a forecast or an expectation. Dates marked 'counted' are the researchers' arithmetic from the act. Entries before 6 October 2026 are the recent dates the guide relies on.

Not establishedOpen questions: what the round did not establish, where it looked, and when to check againForty-four questions a founder would act on, each with what the records do establish as of 6 October 2026, where the answer was looked for, what would close it and a recheck date. They are grouped by the guide section they belong to.
Question 1 · The ladder: what each kind of registration takes and gives

Four rungs: each adds filings, and only the company limits every member's liability

As of 6 October 2026 a person may trade with no Registrar filing; a business name adds €10 and €80 and no yearly return; a partnership €120; a company an advocate, a €165 filing, a yearly return and audit or review. In return the company limits members' liability, within statutory exceptions, and a working shareholder is insured as an employed person.

A natural person may trade in Cyprus without forming a company. The Registrar of Companies' comparison table sets 'unlimited liability of the owner of a business name' against 'limited liability of company members' (read 4 October 2026). The steps are in path 1 (self-employed) and path 2 (company).1

Where a company's limited liability stops

  • Fraudulent trading: where in a winding up business is found carried on to defraud creditors, the Court, on application of the Official Receiver, the liquidator or a creditor or contributory, may declare persons knowingly party to it personally responsible, 'without any limitation of liability', for all or any of the company's debts as it directs (Cap. 113 s. 311).72
  • Tax, since 1 January 2026: officers who bear criminal liability for a company's unpaid tax (for tax it withheld, its executive director, board members and financial officers; for other taxes only if shown to have taken part fraudulently) are also liable jointly or severally with it in civil proceedings (Law 4/1978 s. 51A(3A)); a director deleted from the register stays answerable for liabilities of his term (s. 53A).7374
  • Social insurance and consumer law: an officer whose consent, connivance or neglect lies behind the company's offence is guilty of it too (Law 59(I)/2010 s. 85(9); Law 112(I)/2021 s. 65).7576
  • Beneficial owners: the director or managing director is jointly and/or severally liable for the charge on a company that fails to file (anti-money-laundering (AML) Law s. 61A(10)(ε)).77

The yearly cost of standing still

  • Self-employed, assembled from the Social Insurance Services' 2026 Tables I and II: on the lowest notional minimum (€331.14 a week, category 13, which includes 'persons responsible for providing services and sellers') social insurance comes to €2,858.40 a year, GeSY €688.77 and the training levy from the second quarter €64.57 - about €3,612.7879
  • Shopkeepers' minimum is €452.56 a week (€3,906.48 social insurance a year); that of liberal professionals in their first ten years, designers, computer operators and anyone not classed elsewhere €485.67 (€4,192.32). The base runs from the category minimum unless lower income is proved; form YKA 1-017 is for paying on actual income.65787980
  • Business name: no yearly fee or return at the Registrar. Premises in a municipality, on any rung: a yearly trade fee within ceilings of €50 for self-employed craftsmen, €200 for professionals, traders and businessmen working as individuals and €150-500 for a private company or partnership, by number of employees.1781
  • Company: annual return €20; late, €50 plus €1 a day, at most €150 (the Registrar's fee page still showed the older €500 scheme on 4 October 2026); a municipal legal-person fee with ceilings of €1,000 up to 5 employees and €4,000 where its registered office or management is with a law, accounting or audit firm or an administrative-service provider (Limassol, from 20 June 2023: €222, €127 in a group).34388283
  • Company accounts, per firms: review €600-1,500, audit €1,200-3,500+ (Savva Cyprus, 14 July 2026); a dormant company all-in roughly €1,250-2,150 a year (Zeno, 3 July 2026).84
  • Of 12,583 companies registered in 2022, the Registrar's open data of 29 September 2026 show 7,459 (59.3%) 'registered', 3,532 (28.1%) 'reminder letter sent' - 3,518 of these dated February 2026, the month of its letters on overdue returns and accounts - and 1,010 (8.0%) struck off.85

Path 1 · Trading in one's own name

Path 1: Social Insurance and a tax number; the Registrar only for a trade name

A self-employed person registers with the Social Insurance Services by the day work starts and enters the Tax Register; a trade name adds name approval and form EE1 (€10 and €80). No step found is reserved to an advocate. An EU citizen may start before his registration certificate; a third-country national first needs a status that allows it.

  1. 1Social Insurance registrationRegulations: by the day work starts; portal: number in 1-2 weeks
  2. 2Name approval, for a trade name onlynone published (Registrar and Ministry texts read 4-6 October 2026)
  3. 3Business-name registrationCap. 116: within one month of starting business
  4. 4Tax Register entryTax Department guide: 'may take up to ten (10) days'
  5. 5VAT, when due or by choiceVAT Law: notify within 30 days from the end of the month the threshold was passed, or before the end of the 30 days in which it is expected to be
  6. 6Card acceptance, listed activities onlydecree: within one month of starting

Path 1 in order of doing (as of 6 October 2026)

  1. Social Insurance registrationRegulations: by the day work starts; portal: number in 1-2 weeks
    At the nearest District Social Insurance Office on form YKA 1-013 (self-employed registration) or the joint YKA 1-008. The business portal names YKA 1-008, handed in or posted with an identity card, passport or alien registration certificate (ARC), and says 'the social insurance number is usually given within 1-2 weeks of submission'. The rule (Regulations K.D.P. 167/2017; K.D.P.: the Cyprus numbering of regulatory acts) sets no nationality or residence condition. It counts as training-levy registration too.24808995
  2. Name approval, for a trade name onlynone published (Registrar and Ministry texts read 4-6 October 2026)
    Needed where he has a place of business in Cyprus and trades under a name other than his surname with his forenames or initials. €10 per name, €20 more accelerated; the name stays reserved six months. Online filing needs an account on the gov.cy gateway (CY Login). No document sets an order between this step and Social Insurance registration.112151696
  3. Business-name registrationCap. 116: within one month of starting business
    After approval: form EE1 (the business-name statement) by hand or post, or e-filing with a witness's solemn declaration of the signatures, plus any consent required; €80, €40 more accelerated. The statement gives the name, nature, principal place and start date and, for an individual owner, his names, nationality and usual residence. No advocate's declaration or memorandum is asked; the EE1 criteria name no stamp; the advocates' €9 stamp on this application is charged 'for the filing by an advocate'.11214979899
  4. Tax Register entryTax Department guide: 'may take up to ten (10) days'
    In Tax For All (own account or CY Login): 'register as a new taxpayer'; the number comes by e-mail. A declared trade name needs the business-name certificate attached, so in that case this step follows the one above. No document orders it against Social Insurance registration. The Law sets an individual no day-count deadline; the guide does not say calendar or working days.56100101
  5. VAT, when due or by choiceVAT Law: notify within 30 days from the end of the month the threshold was passed, or before the end of the 30 days in which it is expected to be
    Due for a person established in Cyprus once taxable supplies in the 12 months to a month's end exceed €15,600 (unless the Commissioner accepts the next year stays under the lower limit), or are expected to within 30 days; voluntary on intention. Form T.F. 1101 on paper at a District Tax Office, or by hand or post at the Point of Single Contact. The form puts the tax number first; the web pages accept a pending reference (REGXXX); neither says which applies. No issue time published; late notice €85 a month.4849102103104
  6. Card acceptance, listed activities onlydecree: within one month of starting
    For consumer payments, only if his main activity code is listed in Decree K.D.P. 259/2021 as amended in 2022: most in-store retail, restaurants and bars, and services such as legal, accounting, architects', photography and medical or dental practice; not internet retail (47.91) or computer programming. The month runs from the start of activity; the decree sets no order. JCC's form (v2.3, 4 October 2026) asks for registration, tax and VAT numbers and a current bank account, and charges €17 once.51105106

A business name then carries standing duties under Cap. 116: changes notified within seven days, cessation within one month; letters show the owner's name and, if he is not Cypriot, his nationality. A late notice of a new place of business or changed particulars costs up to €50 plus €1 a day, at most €250; while in default the owner cannot enforce the business's contracts by action without a court's relief.17

An EU citizen's branch

  • He may start before the registration certificate: Law 7(I)/2007 art. 23(1) bars making it a precondition where entitlement can be shown by other means.107
  • If he stays over three months he applies within four months of arrival (fine up to €2,500; fee €20) on form MEU1 (the EU citizen's registration application), in person by appointment: at the Migration Department if he lives in Nicosia district, otherwise at the district police immigration unit. Decision 'within one month at the latest' on a complete application, per the Department; the Law says 'immediately'.108109
  • For the self-employed ground the Department's list (5 October 2026) asks for a certificate of contributions paid for the last four months, or, if he is insured in another EU state, form A1 and health insurance; the Law asks, with an identity card or passport and the €20 fee, only 'proof of self-employment'; the business portal names a certificate of registration as self-employed.110111112113
  • Tax Register: the certificate; without it or a residence permit, category 4 papers - a foreign tax-number certificate, identity card or social-insurance certificate, a photo and a letter of reasons with evidence - plus the fee receipt if he applied. The page (28 September 2026) lists evidence for property, a foreign director, the 60-day rule and employment, none for self-employment, nor says it is accepted.114115
Open look again by 6 Apr 2027

The Department asks a self-employed EU citizen for four months of paid contributions (or form A1 and health insurance if insured in another EU state), while the Law has him apply within four months of arrival; no text read on 5-6 October 2026 reconciles the two periods.108110111

A third-country national needs a status that allows him to run his own business. The Aliens and Immigration Regulations treat it as an 'independent profession', individually or through a company or partnership, needing a permit; a visitor's permit bars any business without the Director's prior written permission; an employment permit allows work only for the named employer. For a non-EU owner the Registrar's EE1 criteria say 'permission is required by the Immigration Officer', without saying what it is.313116117118

At the other counters a third-country national shows his own documents: form YKA 1-013 takes an alien registration or passport number; the Tax Register takes the residence permit, all sides, or, if only applied for, the fee receipt plus the foreign certificate, photograph and letter of reasons.80114

Two or more people trading together register a partnership within one month of formation: name approval, then e-filing or form Σ1 signed by all partners, €120 (€40 more accelerated). Every partner is jointly liable for the firm's debts; limited partners only up to their contribution. A limited partnership is not a separate legal person (Cap. 116 s. 47(6)); the Ministry's 2026 action plan schedules drafting a framework for limited partnerships 'with separate legal personality' (September 2025-January 2027); no such bill was found on the consultation portal, in the Gazette or in CyLaw by 6 October 2026.202124132

Path 2 · The barest company

A private company: advocate-drafted papers and HE1 at the Registrar, then tax, owners, VAT, staff

Formed at the Registrar after name approval, on a memorandum and articles only an advocate may draft; the Registrar's HE1 is an advocate's oath, though the Law also allows a director or secretary. Tax registration via CY Login (within 60 days), beneficial owners (90 days) and VAT when due follow. As of 6 October 2026 no authority publishes processing times.

Forming the company, in the order the Registrar's texts set

  1. Name approvalRegistrar: none published; per firms 3-5 working days or about two weeks standard, 1-4 working days accelerated
    An e-filing user first registers on the gov.cy gateway, whose links lead to CY Login (Registrar page, read 5 October 2026). €10 per proposed name, €20 more accelerated; an approved name stays reserved for six months, within which the incorporation is filed (as of 4 October 2026).152796
  2. Memorandum and articles
    Only a practising advocate may draft them, certifying that he did; a memorandum or articles drafted in breach is void (Advocates Law, Cap. 2, s. 11(5)). The Registrar offers a model memorandum for a general commercial company (2018). His review criteria require the name 'as approved', so the memorandum follows name approval.28147148
  3. Signatures
    The shareholders sign the memorandum and articles in Greek. The memorandum is dated on or before the day HE1 is submitted; the articles bear the same date and the drafting lawyer's name and signature. Online, a witness declares on the Registrar's Annex 'A' that the shareholders and the officer signing forms HE2 and HE3 signed before him, as did the drafting advocate.148149150
  4. HE1 declaration
    HE1, the incorporation declaration form, asks for the name-approval application number; no text read orders it against the signatures. The Registrar's form is an advocate's oath before a District Court registrar (table below); a missing lawyer's stamp is listed first among the 'most common reasons for rejection'.97148151
  5. Filingstatute, online route only: 5 or 10 working days (Cap. 113 s. 366Ε(5)); Registrar: none published
    Any registered e-filing user may submit HE1, the memorandum and articles and the witness's declaration; on paper the Registrar lists HE1, HE2 (office), HE3 (officers) and the memorandum and articles. Fee €165 (€235 without share capital), €100 more accelerated (as of 6 October 2026). The statutory days (5 where only natural persons form it on the Registrar's templates, 10 otherwise) run from completed formalities and payment; if they cannot be met, the Registrar gives the reasons.1631149150
  6. Certificates
    Optional set of five (shareholders, officers, office, memorandum and articles, incorporation): €120, or €130 without a supplied copy, €100 more accelerated (as of 4 October 2026). The tax-register request attaches four.152153154

Path 3 · Selling to consumers online

Selling online to consumers: no licence aimed at it, but site duties, VAT and producer duties

No licence is aimed at selling online. A web shop adds information and withdrawal duties to consumers, product-safety details on each offer, VAT for sales into other EU states (the One Stop Shop only after Cyprus VAT registration) and, where the shop itself imports or first supplies the goods, producer, customs or cosmetics steps.

Pursuing an information-society service needs no prior authorisation, without prejudice to authorisation schemes not aimed specifically at such services (Electronic Commerce Law 156(I)/2004, s. 7(1); in force as read on 5 October 2026). Per the business portal (read 6 October 2026), alcohol and tobacco need a sale licence from the municipality where the premises are, or else the District Officer; food supplements a Ministry of Health notification or, for some products, licence.190191

What the shop's pages and contracts carry

  • The provider's name, geographic address, contact details with e-mail, register and registration number, the supervisory authority where approval is needed, and the VAT number where VAT applies; prices say whether tax and delivery are included (Electronic Commerce Law s. 8).190
  • Per the Consumer Protection Service's page (undated, footer 2022, read 5 October 2026): pre-contract information, confirmation on a durable medium, 14 days to withdraw (from delivery for goods, from the contract for services; up to a year more if the information was not given), refund within 14 days of notice, delivery within 30 days unless agreed. It names no registration and omits the Law's 2026 amendments.192
  • A trader selling goods to consumers shows the selling price and the unit price including VAT and all taxes, in euro; an advertised price comes with its unit price; a reduction states the lowest price of the previous 30 days, save for goods that perish or expire quickly and goods on the market under 30 days (Consumer Protection Law 112(I)/2021, ss. 42-45).193
  • The Consumer Protection Service's Director may fine a breach of that Law up to 5% of the previous year's turnover, or €3,000,000 where turnover is unknown, plus up to €5,000 a day while it continues; recourse does not suspend payment (ss. 57, 61). An officer whose consent, connivance or neglect is shown is also guilty (s. 65).76194

VAT: Cyprus registration first, the One Stop Shop only if chosen

  1. Cyprus VATVAT Law: notify within 30 days after the month the threshold was passed
    For a person established in Cyprus, due once taxable supplies in the past 12 months exceed €15,600 (unless the Commissioner accepts the coming year will stay below the lower limit), or before the end of a 30-day period in which they are expected to exceed it; allowed earlier, on intention. Intra-EU acquisitions of goods above €10,251.61 a calendar year are a separate trigger (Tax Department page, read 4 October 2026).4849102
  2. Sales to consumers elsewhere in the EU
    A seller established only in Cyprus taxes its intra-EU distance sales of goods, and of telecom, broadcasting and electronic services, to consumers in Cyprus while they stay within €10,000 (net of VAT) in the current and the preceding calendar year; above that, at the customer's state's VAT (Directive 2006/112/EC art. 59c, applied from 1 July 2021), as also when the seller opts for it. The One Stop Shop (OSS) is optional: states 'shall permit' traders to use it (art. 369b).199200
  3. OSSRegulation 282/2011 art. 57d: next quarter after notice, or first supply if notified by the 10th of the next month
    OSS uses 'the individual VAT identification number already allocated' (art. 369d), so Cyprus VAT comes first. Sign-up and quarterly returns, due by the end of the month after the quarter, are on the Tax Department's portal tax-oss.mof.gov.cy, per the Commission's Cyprus page, which does not mention Tax For All.199200201202203

The duty to accept cards from consumers turns on the main activity code (Decree K.D.P. 259/2021 under art. 30A of Law 4/1978): most store retail codes 47.11-47.78 are listed, retail via mail order or internet (47.91) is not, and no amending decree adds it (cylaw's indexes to K.D.P. 372/2026, read 6 October 2026). A listed business starting later complies within one month of starting; a virtual POS counts, credit transfers do not.51204205

Path 4 · A shop or a café with premises

A shop needs a municipal licence; a café adds tourism and health approvals and missing use permits

In a municipality a shop needs the s. 56 premises licence (deemed granted after four months' silence on complete papers) and pays a yearly trade fee. A café also needs permits for catering use where the premises lacks them, a sanitary certificate, an approved manager and the Deputy Ministry of Tourism licence; alcohol and sound are licensed apart.

Terms used below: the EOA is the district local-government organisation, which since 1 July 2024 issues building permits and decides planning applications for cafés and most shops; ETEK is the Scientific and Technical Chamber: no one may practise a branch of engineering without registration in its register for that branch, its annual licence and the Greek needed, while its special-list licensees, such as licensed building technicians, may do limited work (Law 224/1990, s. 25); K.D.P. is the Cyprus numbering of regulatory administrative acts. Texts are as read on 5 and 6 October 2026.235236237238239

A shop: what applies (no document sets an order among these)

  • Use class. A building may take another use of the same class without planning permission unless a permit condition bars it; class I is 'shop', excluding hot-food shops, car showrooms and kiosks (General Development Order 2024, K.D.P. 181/2024, para. 5). ETEK and the EOAs apply the Order from 10 May 2024; the Gazette notice its para. 6 ties commencement to was not found.240
  • Change of use. Shop (class I), office (II) and café (III, 'restaurant without music, cafeteria') are different classes and nothing exempts a shop becoming a café, so a shop or office becoming a café needs planning permission, and the change of use a permit obtained in advance (Cap. 96, s. 3(1)(ε)), on the Law's wording even without works. Shops and offices pay restaurants' planning fees (K.D.P. 29/2013, para. 4).240241242
  • Premises licence. A shop, or a small café without performances, in a municipality needs a licence under s. 56 of the Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022, conforming to the planning and building laws; keeping premises without it is punishable by a fine of up to €500. If the municipality does not answer within four months of receiving all documents, 'the licence is deemed to have been granted' (s. 45).243
  • Limassol's s. 56 form for food and drink premises (PDF of 7 October 2024) asks a company's Registrar certificates, the lease or use permission, the building permit, the health certificate and, for most categories, the tourism licence, and runs to 31 December. Neither Limassol's s. 55 and s. 56 forms nor Nicosia's guidance print the licence fee (read 6 October 2026).244
  • Enforcement. Paphos Municipality announced in December 2025 that a survey had found 'over 3,000' premises without the annual licence under ss. 55 and 56 - banks, clinics, professionals' offices and shops among them - and that from 1 March 2026 it would take legal action and immediately suspend every unlicensed premises.245
  • Trade fee. Yearly ceilings for premises in a municipality (s. 56(5), Fifth Schedule): craftsmen €50; individual traders and professionals €200; private companies and partnerships €150 (to 5 employees) to €500 (over 30); insurance, shipping, airline, banking, financing, portfolio and public companies €1,000; others €300. Half in the second half-year; rises capped at 10% a year; councils may exempt kinds of business.81
  • Signs. A 'point of sale' sign about the business carried on in a building and fixed to it needs no council approval if not across the street and within limits on height (15 feet), projection and share of the facade (a fifth) (Cap. 50, s. 6(3)); signs inside a ground-floor shop window are outside the Law. Other signs need approval, decided within four months of complete papers; silence does 'not' grant it (s. 10).246
  • Opening hours, where Part IV of the Shops Law 155(I)/2006 applies (most municipal areas and some communities): a general shop opens no earlier than 5:00 and closes by 19:30 on winter and 20:00 on summer weekdays, by 15:00 on Wednesdays, by 19:00 or 19:30 on Saturdays, and stays shut on Sundays (s. 20); December, the ten days before Easter, special shops and tourist zones fixed by decree are excepted.247248
  • Prices. Goods sold to consumers show the selling and unit price including VAT and all taxes, on the goods, packaging or shelf (Consumer Protection Law 112(I)/2021, ss. 42, 44); a shop serving consumers posts its main services' final prices inside and, where technically feasible, on the front, unless special legislation sets the sector's price information or the service cannot be priced in advance (s. 47).193249
  • Licensed goods, per the business portal (alcohol and tobacco pages last updated 7 December 2023, read 6 October 2026): alcohol and tobacco need a sale licence from the municipality or District Officer (tobacco €51.25 plus €0.85 stamp duty, valid to the next 12 March); food supplements a notification to, or for some products a licence from, the Ministry of Health.191
  • Producers. Packaging-waste costs fall on anyone who makes, imports, transports, supplies or in any way trades packaged products (Law 32(I)/2002, s. 9(1)); a Cyprus firm professionally importing electrical equipment and placing it on the market, or first supplying batteries from abroad, is a producer and enters the Environment Department's register (K.D.P. 73/2015, reg. 21; K.D.P. 125/2009; Regulation (EU) 2023/1542).206213218
  • Fire design. The designer applies Annex IV of the Streets and Buildings Regulations (K.D.P. 400/2020) to developments with no permit or application by 31 August 2020; alterations, additions or repairs to an existing licensed building at least meet its Chapters 7 (evacuation) and 9 (products). Shops need emergency lighting on escape routes, except ground-floor shops under 100 m² of sales area with exits within 15 m.250
  • Cards. A business whose main activity code is listed in Decree K.D.P. 259/2021, including restaurants and bars (56.10, 56.30) and most in-store retail (47.11-47.78), accepts cards for consumers' payments, within one month of starting if it starts after the original deadline (para. 3(δ)); any POS or virtual POS counts, a credit transfer does not; notice of card acceptance is shown at entrance and till (para. 6).51205

A café or restaurant adds the tourism (catering) licence of the Deputy Ministry of Tourism: a restaurant, taverna, cafeteria, bar or similar place serving food or drink for payment may not operate without it (Law 29/1985, s. 6(1)); traditional coffee-shops, take-away-only shops, certain canteens and shops with under 8 m² of service area and no alcohol are excluded (s. 2). The business portal (updated 18 September 2026) grants it only on planning and building permits for the use; for a new or altered building it orders the site owner's steps: planning permission, then the Deputy Ministry's plan approval, then the building permit.251252253

  1. 1Planning permission, where the premises has none for the use
  2. 2Planning fee and decisionregulations: 3 months; silence is not a grant
  3. 3Deputy Ministry of Tourism approves the plansafter the planning permit (portal; Deputy Ministry form)
  4. 4Building or change-of-use permitfor a new or altered building, after the plan approval (portal); Cap. 96 sets no decision time
  5. 5Works, then certificate of approvalstatute: apply within 21 days of finishing
  6. 6Catering manager approved (the founder if he qualifies, or a hired manager)portal: decision within 3 months of a complete application; no fee
  7. 7Sanitary certificate
  8. 8Apply for classification and the catering licenceportal: at least 1 month before opening; decision within 3 months of a complete application
  9. 9Licence granted; fee paidstatute: on the sanitary certificate and the fee (s. 6(3))
  10. 10Municipal licence, in a municipality: s. 55 or s. 56statute: 4 months from complete papers, then deemed granted
  11. 11Alcohol retail licence (Cap. 144)statute: 2 months from complete papers, extendable once, then deemed granted
  12. 12Sound emission licence, where sound may disturb nearby homesstatute: 15-day notice, 15 days for objections, issue within 1 month of a complete application

A café or restaurant: the steps, in order where a document sets one

  1. Planning permission, where the premises has none for the use
    The owner (registered or entitled to be) or his representative applies through an ETEK-licensed designer he authorises; for a company owner all directors or authorised persons sign (Planning Control Manual, January 2025). Online only, in IPPODAMOS, since 1 July 2024 (EOAs' FAQs). Cafeterias, restaurants and bars: decided by the EOA's Head of the Planning Licensing Sector (K.D.P. 350/2026), with the EOA Council's consent if the local authority objected with reasons, failing which the Council decides.237239252254255
  2. Planning fee and decisionregulations: 3 months; silence is not a grant
    Fee on submission (K.D.P. 29/2013; restaurants, catering, shops, offices): €125 per 40 m² of covered space or part, new development; €80 plus €90 per added 40 m², alterations adding space; €110, alterations without; change of use: the new use's fee. Decision or referral to the Minister notified in writing within three months of receipt or a longer period agreed in writing (K.D.P. 62/2016, reg. 6); failing it, appeal to the Council of Ministers as if refused, within 30 days after the deadline (Law 90/1972, s. 32).242256
  3. Deputy Ministry of Tourism approves the plansafter the planning permit (portal; Deputy Ministry form)
    Only for a new or altered building: the owner of the site or building - not the operator - files the plans with the planning permit on form F-KEN-01/1 (business portal, updated 18 September 2026). Nicosia's licence table (2024) also sends the planning permit to the Deputy Ministry for classification and stamping of plans before the building-permit application.253257258
  4. Building or change-of-use permitfor a new or altered building, after the plan approval (portal); Cap. 96 sets no decision time
    The owner's designer files in IPPODAMOS - for a new or altered building, with the plans the Deputy Ministry approved (portal) - and IPPODAMOS computes and collects the fee (EOA FAQs). The issuer is the EOA's Director of Development Licensing (Cap. 96, s. 2), not the municipality named in the Deputy Ministry's 2018 sheet and a Larnaca FAQ. Fire Service conditions go into the permit; cafés and shops stayed under that consultation when an Interior Ministry circular of 14 November 2024 exempted low-risk housing.236238241253255259260
  5. Works, then certificate of approvalstatute: apply within 21 days of finishing
    An owner who does not apply for the certificate of approval within 21 days of finishing gets a notice, and a fine of up to €5,000 only if he does not remedy it in time (Cap. 96, s. 21). The Fire Service's views are sought again for the inspection. No catering licence issues for premises the certificate of final approval deems unsuitable (Law 29/1985, s. 6(7)).236257259
  6. Catering manager approved (the founder if he qualifies, or a hired manager)portal: decision within 3 months of a complete application; no fee
    The manager is a graduate of a recognised hotel or tourism school with knowledge of food and drink, or has a school-leaving certificate and a year's catering experience, or three years' experience the authority accepts (classes A, B: school route only), and of good character (Law 29/1985, s. 16). Application (portal, 2 April 2021): qualifications, experience certificates, criminal record under 365 days old. The licence application carries his details; the licence issues once he is approved (portal).252253261262
  7. Sanitary certificate
    The catering licence issues on a sanitary certificate (Law 29/1985, s. 6(3)) from the Ministry of Health's service or a municipal health service, as the case may be (s. 2). The portal's catering page names the Ministry; Nicosia's guidance (2024) uses a municipal certificate on a €50 prepayment, which the Deputy Ministry also requires.235257263
  8. Apply for classification and the catering licenceportal: at least 1 month before opening; decision within 3 months of a complete application
    The operator applies before operation starts (Law 29/1985, s. 6(2)) with, per the portal (18 September 2026), the title deed, the property owner's solemn declaration, the proposed manager's details, a health certificate, the planning permit for the use and a company's Registrar certificates issued or validated within 60 days - an age limit the Deputy Ministry's own form does not set.251253257264265
  9. Licence granted; fee paidstatute: on the sanitary certificate and the fee (s. 6(3))
    The portal grants it only once the permits for the use are held and the manager approved; the 2018 procedure sheet takes the application after the works even while the building permit is pending. Fee for issue or renewal, by the class the Deputy Ministry assigns: €170 (A), €85 (B), €51 (C) in the Regulations (Law Commissioner's consolidation, archived June 2022); €170.86, €85.43 and €51.26 on the portal (18 September 2026), payable on approval.238252264
  10. Municipal licence, in a municipality: s. 55 or s. 56statute: 4 months from complete papers, then deemed granted
    A restaurant, tavern, snack bar, cafeteria, pizzeria or bar over 50 m², or premises of any size used for performances or public entertainment, needs a prior s. 55 licence; a smaller café without them falls under s. 56. A s. 55 licence needs a building permit and certificates of the Municipal Engineer, the Electrical and Mechanical Services (EMS), the municipality's Fire Service head and the municipal health service. For s. 55 no record sets an order against the catering licence; Limassol's s. 56 form asks for it.243244266267
  11. Alcohol retail licence (Cap. 144)statute: 2 months from complete papers, extendable once, then deemed granted
    Municipal council, or District Officer outside municipalities. Applicant 'of good character' (police certificate) and a 'fit person', premises suitable (s. 5); no legal-form, nationality or residence condition in the Law. Portal list (7 December 2023): municipal sanitary certificate and, where applicable, tourism licence and a criminal record under 3 months old. Yearly fee (portal table): €136.68 in a municipality, €85.43 elsewhere, €341.72 with entertainment by artists; half if granted after 13 September.59263268
  12. Sound emission licence, where sound may disturb nearby homesstatute: 15-day notice, 15 days for objections, issue within 1 month of a complete application
    Needed where the establishment causes or may cause noise nuisance to nearby homes and emits sound beyond its plot; issued by the municipality, or the District Officer outside them, unless a decree names another body (Law 50(I)/2016). The owner posts a 15-day notice of intent; the application carries the planning and/or building permit and the operating licence. No fee regulation is in cylaw's indexes; 2021 draft fees were still pending on 6 October 2026, per Nomoplatform.269270

A planning application for a bar, night club, beer hall, music or dance centre, discotheque and similar uses is first advertised in at least two daily newspapers in the Minister's form, and carries the signer's declaration of publication with proof; the planning authority also consults any local authority that may be affected (K.D.P. 62/2016, regs 5, 7(1)(α)). A cafeteria or restaurant without music is not named, though the authority may add any development (reg. 5(3)(ιβ)). Read 6 October 2026.271

Also for a café; no document sets an order for these

  • Outdoor tables on a pedestrian street need a licence or sub-licence of use from the municipality, 'also for the purposes of outdoor dining' (Law 52(I)/2022, s. 44(1)(ιδ), as substituted by Law 87(I)/2024); the council sets the procedure, documents, conditions (hours, space, furniture, free passage) and fee (s. 46(α)).272
  • Limassol's outdoor-dining form (October 2025) asks the building permit with permitted and current use, plans, any lease and an ID card or passport (for a company, its certificates and the director's ID or passport); Nicosia's (February 2026) permit numbers, photos, an ID-card number with no passport field and a declaration that the applicant is tenant and director. Neither states a fee or time (read 6 October 2026).273
  • Food business registration. A food business operator notifies each establishment for registration (Regulation (EC) No 852/2004, art. 6(2)); the Ministry of Health's form T-Φ-032A/7 (July 2025) goes to the district Public Health Services with a company's incorporation certificate, no fee or time named. It is silent on premises with a municipal health service; Nicosia's table (2024) lists Ministry registration once.230231258
  • Food handlers. Staff handling unpacked food hold a health certificate: after a stool test at their own cost a Chief Medical Officer issues it the same day for €22 plus a registration fee, valid 12 months (portal, 2 May 2024); in a licensed catering establishment every person employed holds a sanitary certificate (Law 29/1985, s. 17(2)).230

Who files what. The site owner, or his representative, files the planning and building-permit applications through an ETEK-licensed designer, and the plans for the Deputy Ministry's approval; that a tenant needs the landlord's authorisation is an inference, not a quoted rule. The operator applies for the catering licence; Limassol's s. 56 form asks the applicant company's certificates and the lease or use permission. Public officers issue the s. 55 certificates, and hired professionals prepare part of what they check: the EMS form needs an electrical designer and a contractor, each with an EMS register number, so a founder without one cannot sign it - an inference from the forms.239244253254255267274275

Source trap

The portal's eligibility rule is not in the Law. The business portal (18 September 2026) grants the catering licence only to persons resident in Cyprus, citizens of another EU state or legal persons situated in one, and asks a non-EU national for a residence and employment permit; Law 29/1985 (cylaw, to Law 170(I)/2020) and its Regulations (2022 archived consolidation), searched on 6 October 2026 for residence, nationality and EU terms, carry no such condition, and the portal cites no section.282283

Not there look again by 6 Jan 2027

No fee or time for the Fire Service certificate of a café over 50 m² (s. 55(2)(δ)) was found on 6 October 2026: cylaw's indexes 2021-2026 hold only staff, discipline and reserve regulations under the Fire Service Law 100(I)/2021, and the two Service pages read describe no certificate a business applies for. Per Nicosia's guidance the Service inspects by appointment and certifies only premises whose plans and conditions it approved at the planning or building-permit stage.235259284

The 2026 catering law. After the Government bill was withdrawn on 19 March 2026, a member's bill by MP Kyriakos Hadjiyiannis, 'Ο περί της Ίδρυσης και Λειτουργίας Χώρων Αναψυχής Νόμος του 2026', was passed by the plenary on 6 April 2026, per Nomoplatform's records. Per press (Dikaiosyni summarising Phileleftheros, 28 April 2026), the President referred it to the court after the Legal Service found that 'a number of its provisions' conflict with the Constitution; no Presidency statement of grounds was found on 6 October 2026.285286

Open look again by 23 Oct 2026

Status on 6 October 2026: passed, referred (per press) and not in CyLaw's 2026 list of laws; Law 29/1985 remains in force. The Supreme Constitutional Court lists presidential references by number only, so which one concerns this law is not established; its October list sets hearings of references on 8, 20 and 23 October, and no date for an opinion is published.257287288

What the 2026 law would change: the bill as tabled, and the passed text as the press reported it

  • As tabled on 26 March 2026: licensing would move from the Deputy Ministry of Tourism to the municipal or community council, merged with the council's leisure licence where both are needed; the licence would issue within two months, valid three years and renewable; Laws 1985-2020 and Regulations 1986-2005 would be repealed. The committee amended the bill before the vote; the passed text was not seen.289
  • Hours, per Ant1's report of the vote (press; passed text unpublished): catering and leisure premises and bars 7.00-2.30 Sunday-Thursday, 7.00-3.30 Friday-Saturday in May-September, to 2.00 and 3.00 in October-April; the District Officer may vary them by special licence. Tabled: 6.00-3.30 (bars 8.00-3.30) all year. Shops Law Part IV does not cover restaurants and leisure premises as to on-premises service (s. 3(2)).248290

Not established in this section

  • Fire Service certificate. What does the Fire Service charge, and how long does it take, for the certificate a café over 50 m2 needs for its municipal licence? look again by 6 Jan 2027
  • Building permit: fee and decision time. What does a building or change-of-use permit cost under the rules in force, and is there a deadline for deciding it? look again by 6 Apr 2027
  • Municipal licence fees. What do municipalities actually charge for the s. 55 and s. 56 premises licences and for outdoor tables? look again by 6 Jan 2027
  • Sound licence: fee and term. What fee and term apply to a café's sound emission licence? look again by 6 Jan 2027
  • Catering licence term. Which term does the Deputy Ministry print on the catering licences it issues: the Law's three years, or the one year of the Regulations and the business portal? look again by 6 Jan 2027
  • The 2026 leisure-premises law. What does the law passed on 6 April 2026 say, why was it referred, and when will the court give its opinion? look again by 23 Oct 2026
  • Food-establishment registration. Does a licensed café also register with the Ministry of Health's register of food establishments, and at what cost and time? look again by 6 Jan 2027

What is known on each point, and where it was looked for, is in the register at the end.

Question 2 · Real businesses opened 2022–2026

Real cases 2022-2026: register and web dates are public; no licence issue date was found

Read from the Registrar's free search, web archives, the press and the tourism lists as of 6 October 2026. Two of the barest businesses were public before their registration; the tourism lists seen print at most a licence's expiry, no issue date; B-READY 2025's 11.5 days for company entry is an expert median, not a case.

Each case is assembled from the Registrar of Companies' free search as served on 6 October 2026, web-archive captures, the businesses' own websites, Wolt's trader panels, the EU's VIES service, the Register of Social Enterprises, the press and the Deputy Ministry of Tourism's lists of catering and entertainment venues. Elapsed times are calendar days between two named dates, start day excluded, counted for this guide, not published. Founders' own accounts are labelled; none is verified.232291292293294295296297298

The Valiotti account describes 2022 rules. A Council of Ministers decision of 30 November 2022, in force 12 December 2022, added proof of an initial investment of at least EUR 200,000 to registration as a company of foreign interests; since 30 June 2026 applications go only through the company's CY Login profile. The Business Facilitation Unit's published time went from 'within seven (7) working days' (page of May 2022) to 'in no more than ten (10) business days' (page modified 23 September 2026).307309310

Company to inauguration: 552 days; TRUE HEART CAFE name to it: 84; social-enterprise entry to it: 23.320321
  • Said (Cyprus Mail, 6 June 2026) by Ellen Georgiou Pontikis, founder of Voice for Autism, the NGO behind the café: 'navigating the complex legal issues because the EU doesn't have a template, it's given to the member states. The legal costs was another issue'; and 'It's more expensive to set up than a traditional business model', citing training, possibly an adaptive workspace, an in-house support team. No amounts.322
  • Said (same article): Head of Operations Alexandros Karpis: 'Usually starting out in hospitality takes anywhere between six months to two, three years to start first operations. We went very quickly. We've got help from government, we've got help from private investors.' A general statement, not a measured time for this café; it names no steps, permits or licences, and 'first operations' is not defined.323
  • Not seen: no public source found dates the licences, bank account or card terminal; the lists do not say whether a licence was issued, transferred or amended.320321

  • LEVASCO CONCEPT LTD, ΗΕ 452057, registered 4 October 2023, owns the business name SUNDAY IN LISBOA CONCEPT STORE, ΕΕ 58259, registered 13 days later: a fashion boutique with a Portuguese café corner at 203 Makariou III Avenue, Limassol, whose website sells with worldwide shipping.298324

Premises, café: Rincon Latino, Nicosia (no tourism-list entry found)

In outline (assembled from these records): etxetera, a Nicosia café and shop whose company was registered on 25 January 2026, launched 'earlier this month' per an article of 19 March 2026, 35-53 days later; it is on no Nicosia tourism list dated 16/02/2026 to 11/08/2026 by name, and no source read gives its address, so an entry under another name could not be looked for. How to read the register

  • The free search shows number, type, status, registration date, directors and secretary (or a business name's owner), address, 'pending services' with application dates, the date the last HE32 was registered and lodged HE32s with made-up dates; no shareholders (6 October 2026). Monthly open-data files on data.gov.cy were last modified 29 September 2026.291
  • Registration dates include weekends: in the Registrar's open-data file of 29 September 2026, 2,647 of 16,780 companies registered in 2025 (15.8%) carry a Saturday or Sunday date, against 6.5% for 2023 and 9.2% for 2024 (a count made for this guide, companies since struck off included); so elapsed times are counted in calendar days.332
  • Every company with share capital delivers its annual return within 28 days of the date it is made up to (Companies Law s. 120(1)); the first reference date is the day after 18 months from incorporation (s. 120(1A)(a)). Applications came 61 days after the made-up date at KFB Hospitality Concepts Ltd, 221 and 77 days at N.N. Cyber Digital Products Ltd, and 293 days at Kuns Studio Ltd (not shown here).34314317
  • The free search cannot find business names by their owner: names held under other names cannot be searched by owner. It returns at most 200 results per search, and no details page opens outside a search (6 October 2026).291331
Source trap

A pending HE32 is a lodged return, not a registered one. On 6 October 2026 nine HE32 applications of five companies followed in the research (the three above, plus Kuns Studio Ltd and J.P Mojo Design Limited, whose application of 17 November 2023 is the oldest, 1,054 days) sit both under 'pending services' and in the HE32 archive, with the date of the last HE32 registration empty; in a spot check of eight unrelated companies with any HE32, seven show the same. The search does not say what 'pending' means.305333334

How to read the tourism lists

  • The Deputy Ministry of Tourism publishes one list per district, on gov.cy (Greek, dated 19/06/2026) and visitcyprus.com (English editions, the newest seen a Nicosia list dated 11/08/2026): trade name, category, address, mostly a telephone, and in Greek editions from 06/11/2025 a licence-expiry column, blank for some rows. None seen on 6 October 2026 names a holder or gives a licence number or issue date.293335
  • Older editions sit on visitcyprus.com, newer ones on gov.cy. The Nicosia list of 06/11/2025 survives only as a web-archive copy of 14 November 2025, its gov.cy address answering 'not found' (HTTP 404) on 6 October 2026; the Limassol list of that date also survives as a web-archive copy of a gov.cy file.335336
Source trap

A list date bounds a change, it does not date it. Each café's name replaced an entry listed at that address for at least two and a half years, and two of the three new entries kept the earlier venue's telephone numbers. The lists do not say whether an entry was renamed, transferred or newly issued.326328337

An aggregate, not a case: the World Bank's B-READY 2025, the first edition to cover Cyprus (report of 29 December 2025), gives 11.5 calendar days for 'the entire company entry process', domestic and foreign-owned alike, at 1,920 euro (domestic) and 1,750 (foreign). These are medians of expert answers as of 1 September 2024 for the most common limited company in the largest city, with employees and turnover above the VAT threshold, not register measurements; cost is official fees plus the experts' estimate where a step has none, VAT excluded, a lawyer only if mandatory.183184

Reproducibility package, files of 14 April 2026. No bank account or general licence is counted; some steps are marked as done at the same time.

Source trap

The published total is not the sum of the steps: each figure is a separate median, so the per-step medians sum to 20.5 days and 2,055, and the questionnaire's own sum-of-steps field gives 21.5 days and 1,885. For a foreign-owned company the experts report no additional or differing step, yet the published foreign total is 1,750.186

What the B-READY figures leave out

  • The bank account: the experts' median answer to whether opening one is required by law or commonly done in practice to start a domestic company is No, so it is not in the 11.5 days and 1,920. The questionnaire counts the step only where needed for entry, such as depositing paid-in minimum capital, and says to answer No where an account is opened only for operational reasons.187
  • Per-step data from 2026: the Methodology Handbook's Third Edition (January 2026) asks only for total time and cost, so B-READY 2026 data can carry no per-step time for Cyprus.338
  • Foreign owners: the experts' answer that foreign entrepreneurs face no screening different from domestic ones (reference point 1 September 2024) predates Law 194(I)/2025, in force since 2 April 2026, which requires approval of some non-EU investments.189

Not established in this section

  • Founders' own dated accounts. How long did each step take, in the founders' own words, for businesses registered in 2022-2026? look again by 6 Apr 2027
  • Licence dates of premises cases. When were the case cafés and shops licensed? look again by 6 Apr 2027

What is known on each point, and where it was looked for, is in the register at the end.

Question 3 · Who to hire, what they close, what it costs

Only an advocate may draft a company's founding documents; later routine filings name no lawyer

Cyprus law reserves drafting a company's memorandum and articles to a practising advocate, audits to licensed auditors, plans to registered engineers and architects, and director, secretary and office services offered to others to eligible persons. Firms publish formation prices on different bases as of 6 October 2026; none is an official fee.

Acts the law reserves, and what the founder may do himself

ActWho may do it, and the instrumentThe founder himself
Drafting the memorandum and articles, or a resolution on the company's organisationA practising advocate only (Advocates Law, Cap. 2, ss. 2(1), 11(1)); a memorandum drafted otherwise is void (s. 11(5)). Unlicensed practice (s. 11(3)) and undertaking or advertising to draft one (s. 11(5)(ε)) are offences.No. He signs before a witness, for whom neither the Companies Law nor the Registrar's forms set a qualification.28339340341342
Declaration of compliance, form HE1 (the incorporation declaration)By the Companies Law (Cap. 113, s. 17(2)), the formation advocate or a person named in the articles as director or secretary; the Registrar's form is worded only for the advocate.By Cap. 113, s. 17(2), yes, if so named, and s. 37A(4) lets the declaration be filed electronically. But the Registrar's incorporation page asks on both routes for HE1 sworn by the entrusted lawyer; no Registrar announcement of September 2003 to 30 September 2026 says a director may make it, and firms disagree.29151157158
Audit or review; books; tax computationsAudit or review: a licensed statutory auditor or audit firm (Law 53(I)/2017, s. 33(1); Cap. 113, s. 152A(1)(d)). From 1 January 2026 the Tax Commissioner may disregard tax computations not certified by an ICPAC (Institute of Certified Public Accountants) practising-certificate holder or other recognised body (Law 4/1978, s. 29).Not the audit or review. Cap. 113 puts the books on the directors and no provision of it requires a licensed accountant (s. 141(1)). A sole trader with turnover and other gross income up to €120,000 is exempt from accounts that must be audited or reviewed (Law 4/1978, art. 30, from tax year 2026); he still keeps books.11343344345
Director, secretary or registered office as a serviceEligible persons only (Law 196(I)/2012, ss. 4(1), 5(1)): CySEC (Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission) licensees, advocates and law firms, ICPAC members and their firms. Every company keeps a registered office in Cyprus (Cap. 113, s. 102); whether a founder giving his own address 'provides' it, the Act does not say.Exempt as director if he or his family own 25%+, or, not controlling its board, of under ten companies; if resident, as secretary if they own 50%+ (25% if all shareholders are Cyprus-resident individuals) or it is his sole employer; only if not advertised or offered to others (s. 4(3)). None covers an address.161163164165
Engineering studies and plans; planning applicationA person on ETEK's register for the branch, with ETEK's annual licence and the Greek needed (ETEK, the Scientific and Technical Chamber: Law 224/1990, s. 25(1)). Planning: the owner or his authorised representative applies, through a designer the owner authorises (Manual of Planning Control, January 2025).No, unless so registered. ETEK special-list licensees, such as licensed building technicians, may do limited work on buildings of up to two floors and set volumes (s. 25(6)-(7)). That a tenant needs the landlord's authorisation and a designer is an inference from the Manual.239254
Electrical installation of premisesCap. 170, s. 12 lets the Council of Ministers empower the Electrical and Mechanical Services (EMS) Director, another person or a board to license and register electricians and contractors. Designer and contractor each sign form EMS 60.18-1 with an EMS register number; an EMS inspector inspects and signs (Nicosia guidance, 2024).Per the Nicosia guidance, €30.50 is paid at EMS offices with application form EMS 53.1.23 for the inspection. That he cannot sign the declaration unregistered is an inference from the forms.274275

Statutes as consolidated on cylaw, read 4-6 October 2026. A sole director may be secretary only in a single-member company (Cap. 113, s. 171(1)).

Open look again by 6 Apr 2027

Prescribed, not in force on 6 October 2026: K.D.P. 368/2018 sets a new form HE1 whose compliance declaration is made only by 'a practising advocate' entrusted with the formation, with his Bar register number; a proposed director or secretary signs a separate declaration as 'authorised to submit this form'. It applies only once the Registrar brings it into force by Gazette notice; the 2021 notices do not cover HE1 and cylaw's indexes to 18 September 2026 show no later one.155

What the founder can file himself, and where (Registrar's and Tax Department's texts, October 2026)

  • Name approval and online incorporation: the Registrar's e-filing, entered with a CY Login account. Any registered user may submit, but the file carries HE1 sworn by the entrusted lawyer. €10 a name; €165 to register a company with share capital (€235 without).2796150
  • A business name, after name approval: form EE1 by hand or by post, or online as a registered e-filing user with a witness's solemn declaration of signatures, plus any authority's consent the name or the business requires; €80 (+€40 accelerated), within one month of starting business. The guidance asks for no advocate's declaration and no memorandum.14346
  • Changes of directors or secretary (HE4) and share-transfer notices (HE57): within 14 days, online or by hand or post, €20 each (+€20 accelerated); the guidance names no lawyer. The annual return (HE32): e-filing only, with the previous year's financial statements, €20 (+€20 accelerated); its review criteria ask for an officer's signature.3497341
  • Beneficial owners (UBO): per the Registrar's guidance, filed free, only by the company's own officer or partner, not by a service provider unless itself an officer; the Directive (K.D.P. 112/2021) asks only electronic filing with access codes the entity obtains. A director without a Cypriot identity card cannot use his own CY Login; the company's profile, verified in person, or a legal-person officer's remains.22170
  • Tax registration of a company: only through the Tax For All (TFA) portal with CY Login, since 1 July 2026. VAT registration: printed form T.F. 1101 at a District Tax Office or, per the business portal, at the Point of Single Contact. Filing VAT returns for another needs a TFA 04 'representative' listing, no professional qualification.103154347

The advocates' stamp is an Advocates' Pension Fund fee under Regulations made under s. 27 of the Advocates Law. Regulation 3(3), inserted by K.D.P. 103/1988 (K.D.P.: the Cyprus numbering of regulatory administrative acts) and not rewritten since, charges it 'for the filing by an advocate' with the Registrar. The Table (K.D.P. 605/2007, from 1 January 2008; these items not changed by the 2017-2023 amendments) sets €40 on the founding document of a limited company with capital up to €2,000, €26 for a partnership, and €9 on a business-name application, HE32, HE2 (change of registered office) and HE4.9899348349350351352353

Regulation 3(3) charges the stamp on filings by an advocate and names no fee on these forms filed by the founder or an officer himself. Of the Registrar's review-criteria pages (2019), only the company-registration page names a stamp, on HE1, listing a missing stamp first among the 'most common reasons for rejection'; the criteria for HE2, HE4, HE32 and EE1 name none, and those forms have no stamp field.9799

Open look again by 6 Jan 2027

Not tested as of 6 October 2026: whether the Registrar's e-filing system charges the stamp on, or refuses, an HE32, HE2, HE4 or business-name application the founder files himself. The Regulations, review criteria and forms read do not show it, and no Registrar announcement of September 2003 to 30 September 2026 deals with stamps on self-filed forms. How the stamp is collected on an e-filed incorporation was not established either.9799158354

Hiring in writing, and complaining

  • Lawyers have had no minimum fees for out-of-court work since 29 June 2018, when K.D.P. 172/2018 repealed the minimum-fee regulations of 1985-2017. Under K.D.P. 171/2018 an advocate must tell the client in advance how the fee will be set, 'especially' when hourly, and deliver a fee account within a reasonable time and at the latest one month after the client asks; breach is a disciplinary offence.399
  • The written appointment in an out-of-court matter: an 'Advocate Appointment Form' or agreement the client signs, stating the matter, the agreed fee and how it is paid (Annex I to K.D.P. 171/2018), releases the advocate from the regulations' reasonable-fee criteria. An advocate's licence is issued or renewed only with professional-negligence insurance (Cap. 2, s. 6E(1)).400401
  • A lawyer's conduct: a written complaint to the Advocates' Disciplinary Board, €68 fee, for fraudulent, disgraceful or unprofessional conduct or breach of the conduct rules; mishandling a case is not itself an offence. A private complaint proceeds only with the Board's leave, and if the advocate is acquitted the complainant may be ordered to pay costs (Cap. 2, s. 17).402403
  • An accountant: ICPAC, only for those on its registers, filed on its website with a €200 fee; it imposes disciplinary penalties only and leaves compensation to the courts. An auditor or audit work: the Cyprus Public Audit Oversight Board.404
  • A fee dispute in an out-of-court matter: a Bar committee of three advocates under K.D.P. 171/2018, whose decisions have the status of arbitral awards enforceable through a District Court.402
Source trap

The Bar's public page 'Inadequate Professional Services', read 6 October 2026, still gives the Disciplinary Board's fine limit as one thousand pounds. Cap. 2, s. 17 (cylaw text through Law 17(I)/2024) lets the Board warn or reprimand an advocate, fine him up to €20,000, suspend his licence or strike him off; costs ordered against a complainant are assessed on the €10,000-€50,000 scale of civil actions.403

The foreign element · When the owner is foreign

A foreign founder files the same company forms; permits, papers, screening and banks add the rest

The Registrar's criteria identify founders by passport or identity number and ask for no residence permit; per an agency report, she seeks other services' views on companies with Turkish or Turkish Cypriot officers. The foreign element shows mainly in the right to run a business, papers from abroad, branches, screening, land, sanctions and banks.

The Registrar's review criteria (read 5 October 2026) identify an individual director or secretary by 'identity or passport number, country of origin, date of birth and profession', and a shareholder by address, identity number, nationality and profession. No residence permit, registration certificate or Cyprus address of the person is asked for; only the registered office must be in Cyprus. The wording is the same for an EU citizen and a third-country national. An outline assembled from the Companies Law and the immigration texts read on 5 October 2026 found no approval needed to hold shares or to be a director; what is regulated is activity.162405

Source trap

Per a Cyprus News Agency report, the Registrar told a House committee on 3 July 2025 that she asks other services for views on companies with Turkish nationals or Turkish Cypriots among their officers. For 2023 to mid-2025: with Turkish nationals 30 registered, 7 rejected, 21 withdrawn 'mainly because of the delay' in the reply, 13 pending; with Turkish Cypriots 41 registered, 10 rejected, 16 pending; 20 more with other third-country persons rejected.406

Who may run a business: residence statuses by name (in depth on the Cyprus banking page)

  • EU or EEA citizen: per the Migration Department, Union citizens 'enjoy free access to employment, including employed or self-employed activity'. One staying over three months registers within four months of arrival (€20), but the certificate may 'in no case' be made a precondition where entitlement can be shown by other means (Law 7(I)/2007, arts 10, 23(1)).107108
  • Third-country national: long-term residents; family of an EU citizen or a Blue Card holder; a Cypriot's spouse or partner, or a minor Cypriot's parent (policy, after a residence and employment permit); those under international or (on conditions) temporary protection; Startup Visa founders in their company (scheme stated valid to December 2026); immigration permit holders (A-D); Regulation 12 permit holders.3119120121122123124126
  • Not enough: a visitor's permit; a permit naming an employer (work there only); the Blue Card; the Digital Nomad permit (no Cyprus employers or clients). Pupil's, student's, visitor's, employment and other special permit holders may not seek the Regulation 12 permit in Cyprus. Investor permit (policy): employment only as director of the company invested in; if not invested in shares, shareholder and unpaid director.116117122128131407
  • A third-country national who finished studies in Cyprus at master's level or above may stay twelve months 'to seek employment or set up a business' (Law 7(I)/2019, art. 25), applying at least 30 days before the study permit expires; after three months proof of a genuine chance may be asked.130

Papers from abroad

  • Translation: foreign-language official documents enter public registers after translation by a sworn translator (Law 45(I)/2019, s. 18); the Registrar's pages also accept a Greek translation 'by an affidavit in court'. Since 25 July 2025 Cap. 113 (ss. 365ΙΑ-365ΙΒ) has the Registrar issue, on application, English-language certificates or certified copies admissible in any legal proceedings as equal to the original.418419
  • Certification: the Bar's AML Directive (August 2023) gives advocates a 'suggested (non-exhaustive)' list for a corporate client, Cypriot or foreign, including evidence of good standing, certified by a notary, a Hague apostille, a regulated professional in the EU or an equivalent or FATF state, or a Cyprus embassy or consulate.420
  • Directive (EU) 2025/25 (in force since 30 January 2025) has national measures apply from 31 July 2028: an EU Company Certificate 'accepted in all Member States as sufficient evidence' of incorporation, and register-certified copies freed from legalisation, apostille included. Transposition is due by 31 July 2027; on 6 October 2026 no Cyprus law was found (CyLaw's 2025-2026 lists; EUR-Lex: 0 measures).421422423

Directors and the company's tax residence

  • From 1 January 2026 a company is Cyprus tax resident if managed and controlled in Cyprus or incorporated there, unless a tax treaty provides otherwise (Law 244(I)/2025). Form T.D.98 asks whether most board meetings are held, key decisions taken and minutes kept in Cyprus, and most directors are tax resident there. Certificates: treaty countries only; the page does not say what a company incorporated abroad submits.424425426
  • Under the Estonia-Cyprus convention, a company resident in both states under their laws meets no automatic tie-breaker: the authorities settle it 'by mutual agreement', with regard to the place of effective management or any other relevant criterion; Estonia's reservation on MLI Article 4 leaves this in place.427

A branch of a foreign company

  • A foreign company files within a month of setting up a place of business (Cap. 113, s. 347(1)), naming a Cyprus resident to accept service; forms AE1-AE3 cost €380, plus €100 accelerated (6 October 2026). Guidance: true copies of the constitution, apostilled (non-Hague countries: competent authority), translated into Greek unless in Greek or English (the criteria omit the exception). No maximum age is stated.428429
  • A branch is not a new legal entity. It files home and branch accounts yearly, subject to exemptions (s. 350). Managed and controlled abroad, the company is taxed as a non-resident on the branch's profits at 15% and 'may elect' resident treatment; managed and controlled in Cyprus, it is resident. No charge on remitting branch profits was found in the income tax or defence contribution laws.430431432
  • By statute, online registration of an overseas company's branch is completed within 10 working days (Cap. 113, s. 366Η(6), inserted by Law 151(I)/2023).31
  • The Registrar's page 'After the establishment of place of business' (read 6 October 2026, citing no law) gives an overseas company sixty days from registration to register with the Tax Department. Law 4/1978, s. 5A(2), sets 60 days from a company's incorporation or registration in Cyprus from 1 January 2026; since 1 July 2026 overseas companies (AE numbers) apply only through CY Login.32433434
Source trap

  • Since 2 April 2026 (Law 194(I)/2025) the Finance Ministry must first approve a deal where a foreign investor (not an EU, EEA or Swiss national, or a third-country undertaking; residence not mentioned) takes 25% or more, worth €2,000,000 or more with the same parties' 12-month deals, in a strategic-importance target; crossing 25% or 50% in such a target needs notice at any value. Not notifying: €5,000-50,000 fine.435436437438
  • A greenfield investment does 'not satisfy the statutory conditions for mandatory notification', though it may be examined within 15 months of completion where security or public order may be affected; strategic importance turns on 'the actual activities' in Cyprus (guidance, 28 July 2026).   • Under Cap. 109 an 'alien' needs the Council of Ministers' prior permission to acquire immovable property other than on death. Aliens include non-citizens, foreign companies and companies where aliens hold half or more of directors, votes, shares or control; not EU or EEA citizens, legal persons of another EU state seated in the EEA, 'alien Cypriots' or a citizen's non-citizen wife not separated by court decision.441442
  • Acquisition includes a lease over 33 years (or extendable past it by unilateral options), or over ten years for land beyond a home's or premises' needs and in any case over two donums, and a share making a property-holding Cyprus company alien-controlled; on the text an ordinary commercial tenancy needs no permission. The committee chair said it would return to the subject in October 2026, including rules for companies; no session date was found by 6 October 2026.445446447

Sanctions

  • Regulation (EU) No 833/2014 bars, since 24 October 2025, crypto-asset services, payment instruments, acquiring, payment initiation and e-money for Russian nationals, residents and entities (art. 5b(2)), and since 26 February 2022 deposits over €100,000 per bank from them or non-EU entities over 50% owned by them (art. 5b(1)). EU, EEA and Swiss nationals and residence-permit holders are exempt.450451452
  • Since 27 March 2023 Russian nationals and residents may not sit on governing bodies of owners or operators of critical infrastructures and critical entities (art. 5o), only EU, EEA and Swiss nationals exempt; not a general bar on Russians directing EU companies. Violations are crimes (Law 149(I)/2025), and under the Central Bank's 2020 directive banks screen directors, owners and signatories before any service.453454455
  • Trusts and similar arrangements whose trustor or beneficiary is a Russian national, resident or entity may not be registered or given an address or management services (since 9 April 2022), and since 5 July 2022 no one may act as their trustee, nominee shareholder, director or secretary (art. 5m of Regulation (EU) No 833/2014). EU, EEA and Swiss nationals and residence-permit holders are exempt.456
  • Since 25 August 2026 Russian nationals and residents of Russia may not own or control, or sit on the governing bodies of, an EU legal person providing crypto-asset services (art. 5b(2a), as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1848); from 18 January 2024 the bar covered only wallet, account and custody providers. EU, EEA and Swiss nationals and residence-permit holders there are exempt.457

Why · The reasons behind the changes

Why rules changed: reasons sit in bills, committee reports and speeches; some changes state none

Stated reasons come from Government reports to the House, MPs' memoranda, committee reports, a Minister's speech and the Fiscal Council; press accounts fill gaps. The 15% corporate rate has two accounts. The 2026 strike-off drive, the 2018 shell-company circular and the minimum-wage decree state no reason.

What is coming · Pending and planned

What is coming: Cyprus bills mostly undated, EU dates fixed, several transpositions late

As of 6 October 2026 the Cyprus changes that touch a founder are bills, drafts or plans, and few have a dated next step. EU acts set fixed dates; for consumer credit, the single permit, pay transparency and beneficial-owner register access the Cyprus deadline had passed with no law found. Nothing here is in force unless a row says so.

Source trap

A 'pending' label does not prove a bill is alive. Under rule 84B of the House's Rules of Procedure (unofficial codification of January 2020; later amendments of the Rules not checked), members' bills pending in committee at the end of a term whose discussion had not begun, and those of MPs not re-elected, are deemed withdrawn when the new term starts; the rule names only members' bills. A 2025 member's bill fixing sound licences at three years is still shown pending on Nomoplatform but has probably lapsed.278279

VAT in the digital age, Directive (EU) 2025/516.Article 2 from 1 January 2027: the EUR 10,000 threshold counts only goods dispatched from home; union one-stop-shop sellers deemed to opt for destination VAT.
