Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853.Transpose by 9 December 2026; where the manufacturer is outside the EU the importer and the authorised representative answer, or failing both the fulfilment service provider; if no EU operator can be identified, a distributor that does not name one or its supplier within a month of a request answers.Bill consulted February-March 2026; no law in CyLaw's 2026 list.560561
Consumer Credit Directive (EU) 2023/2225.Applies 20 November 2026: third-party 'buy now, pay later' in scope; a shop's own deferral with no third party offering credit, free of interest and charges except limited late-payment charges, paid within 50 days of delivery (14 for online sellers that are not small or medium-sized enterprises), stays outside.Due 20 November 2025; no law in CyLaw's lists.562
Pay Transparency Directive (EU) 2023/970.Due 7 June 2026: pay information for job applicants, no questions on pay history, no size threshold.Draft consulted in 2025; not enacted (none in CyLaw's 2026 laws).563

Company-law Directive (EU) 2025/25.Transpose by 31 July 2027, apply 31 July 2028: EU Company Certificate, digital power of attorney, no apostille on register copies.No law found in CyLaw's 2025-2026 lists or on EUR-Lex; nothing changes for founders before 31 July 2028.422423565

Packaging Regulation (EU) 2025/40.Applies 12 August 2026: producers register in each state where they make packaging available and may not sell unregistered (a producer responsibility organisation they entrust registers unless the state says otherwise); national registers follow within 18 months of an implementing act due by 12 February 2026.No register found (Department of Environment, Green Dot); the Commission's draft act closed for comments on 10 September 2026 and was not adopted on 6 October 2026.209210
Source trap

The EUR 3 duty is not per article. Per the Commission's guidance of 2 June 2026, which says it is explanatory and not legally binding, an item is goods in a consignment sharing tariff classification, description and, where given, origin, and because of IT limits the duty applies per declaration line irrespective of the quantity on it, provided the declaration is worth up to EUR 150 in total.559568

ProposalWhat it would changeStatus and next date
EU Inc., the '28th regime' company.Proposed EU company form (Commission, 18 March 2026): no minimum capital, at least one director resident in the Union, online formation on EU templates with registration within 48 hours for at most EUR 100.In committee; the 19 October 2026 plenary date is a forecast, not a scheduled vote.569570
PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation.Per the Council's release on the provisional agreement (agreed texts not read): firms providing card acceptance make their fees clear; trading name must match statements; cash without purchase, by chip and PIN, up to EUR 150.Agreed provisionally 27 November 2025; indicative plenary 14 December 2026.571572
Digital euro.Payees must accept it; a micro business may refuse unless it accepts comparable digital means such as debit cards.Council position 19 December 2025, Parliament mandate 9 July 2026; not adopted.573

Suspending the authorised-representative duty of extended producer responsibility (EPR).Would suspend until 1 January 2035 the duty of a producer established in one EU state to appoint an authorised representative when selling packaging, batteries or electrical equipment to end users in another; states could still require one of third-country producers.Proposed 10 December 2025; per the Parliament's Legislative Train (20 September 2026), Council talks discontinued and a committee vote planned for early October 2026; not adopted.226

Not established in this section

  • Startup Visa after 2026. Will the Startup Visa continue after December 2026, and on what terms? look again by 31 Dec 2026
  • Golden visa tightening. What will the announced tightening of the investment residence route contain, and when? look again by 6 Jan 2027
  • Committee dates of pending bills. When will House committees take up the land-purchase bills, the national-security Companies bill and the pension bill? look again by 31 Oct 2026
  • Small-entity reporting standard. When will the national reporting standard for small entities be published, so that Law 2(I)/2026 starts? look again by 6 Jan 2027
  • EU wallet deadline. Does Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1731 move the 24 December 2026 date by which each state must provide an EU Digital Identity Wallet? look again by 24 Dec 2026
  • Payments package dates. From when would PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation apply? look again by 14 Dec 2026
  • Signature certification bill. Has the bill moving signature certification from certifying officers to Citizen Service Centres been tabled, and from when would it apply? look again by 6 Apr 2027
  • Packaging producer register. When will Cyprus open its register of packaging producers under Regulation (EU) 2025/40? look again by 6 Apr 2027

What is known on each point, and where it was looked for, is in the register at the end.

Calendar to 2028: fixed deadlines of adopted acts and meetings where change may be announced

Each entry says whether it is a date set by an adopted act, a meeting at which something may be announced, a forecast or an expectation. Dates marked 'counted' are the researchers' arithmetic from the act. Entries before 6 October 2026 are the recent dates the guide relies on.

Open questions: what the round did not establish, where it looked, and when to check again

Forty-four questions a founder would act on, each with what the records do establish as of 6 October 2026, where the answer was looked for, what would close it and a recheck date. They are grouped by the guide section they belong to.

Look again bySectionQuestionEstablished so farWould close it

What does the law passed on 6 April 2026 say, why was it referred, and when will the court give its opinion?		Only the bill as tabled has been read; the House committee amended it, and per press the passed text changes opening hours. Per press, the President referred it to the court after the Legal Service found that 'a number of its provisions' conflict with the Constitution; neither source names them. 6 Apr 2027LadderFounder's unemployment benefit
Can a founder employed by his own company draw unemployment benefit while the company still exists?		Self-employed periods do not count towards unemployment benefit (Social Insurance Law 59(I)/2010, s. 24(2)(α)); a shareholder working in his own private company is insured as employed (First Schedule, Part I, para. 5). A day counts as unemployment only if the claimant proves he is unemployed, capable of and available for work (or in approved training); a day of gainful occupation does not count unless he could normally do it besides his usual work, outside its hours, and earns no more than a prescribed amount that day (s. 31(4)).4463Social Insurance Services guidance or decisions, or court judgments on owner-employees.Looked: Social Insurance Law 59(I)/2010, ss. 24 and 31 and the First Schedule (consolidated text, 6 October 2026); the Social Insurance Services' guides for insured persons and employers.

Fees are set in regulation 62 and Annex II of the Streets and Buildings Regulations, a system the Interior Ministry calls 'complex'; a 2026 draft would replace them with flat rates per m2 but is 'under processing'. Cap. 96, scanned for day and month limits, sets no time for deciding an application. A planning authority gives written notice of its decision within three months, or longer if agreed in writing, and silence is not a grant (K.D.P. 62/2016). Does the Migration Department issue an EU citizen's registration certificate (MEU1) to a self-employed person with fewer than four months of contributions, within the four months from arrival in which he must apply?		Outline from the texts read on 6 October 2026: the certificate is applied for within four months of arrival and may not be made a condition for exercising a right provable by other means (Law 7(I)/2007, arts 10(1), 23(1)); the Law asks only 'proof of self-employment', while the Department's MEU1 list asks for four months of paid contributions (or, if insured in another EU state, form A1 and health insurance). Method · How this page was built

Memory first, then the documents, every fact attacked, every item checked

The guide is a view of memory records. Each record is one checked statement with its source, and the guide says nothing that a record does not carry.

What adversarial checking did to the 385 researcher facts

Sixteen research slices in three waves; each slice read again by two verifiers whose task was to refute it.

Confirmed as written — 104 (27.0%) Corrected: qualifier, status, date, act or scope — 277 (71.9%) Refuted — 4 (1.0%)

The verifiers also added 94 facts of their own; six facts were dropped by decision. With three corrected editions of earlier records that makes 472 records stored.

What the checkers did to the 548 items of this page

Seven writers wrote the sections from the records only; seven checkers compared every item with the records it cites.

Confirmed as written — 331 (60.4%) Corrected — 198 (36.1%) Dropped — 19 (3.5%)

The checkers also added 30 items from records the writers had not used.

Order of work. Memory was asked first: ten narrow questions, three answered (company steps, the online shop, café licences), five in part (the self-employed, the lawyer's role, upkeep prices, the foreign element, what is coming), two not at all (reasons for reforms, real cases). The web part then ran in three waves. The first covered the ladder, cases, whom to hire, the foreign element, reasons and what is coming; the second the order of steps and times, premises costs, a second pass on cases and hiring, and what each rung gives; the third the registrations of a seller of goods, founders' own accounts, and the practical points of the barest path: bank accounts, CY Login and the advocates' stamp.

What the verifiers corrected. Few facts were wrong outright; most lost a condition on the way. The common faults were a qualifier dropped while shortening, an inference stated as a finding, an official guide used without checking that it predates a rule change, and a negative wider than the search behind it. One refuted claim, that the World Bank publishes no per-step figures for Cyprus, led to the per-step data now in the cases section.

From records to page. After each batch the stored text, tags and source of every record were compared with the prepared files byte by byte: 472 of 472 identical. Five earlier records were superseded because this round showed them wrong or incomplete in a way that misleads; three of them were replaced by corrected editions. The checkers of this page found the same kind of error as the verifiers: compression that drops a qualifier, widens a negative or sets an order of steps that no document sets.

Limits. This is a reference study, not legal, immigration or tax advice. Firms' prices are their own published prices on the dates given, and packages include different things; times are what an authority, a provider or a firm publishes; nothing is added up into a total cost or time. Cases rest on public registers, the businesses' own pages and press or founders' accounts; no public source gave the issue date of any café's licence. Greek-language acts were read in Greek, and quotes from them are this study's rendering.

  23. What a Cyprus partnership owes each year. It keeps books (Cap. 116, s. 64). Only where the sole or all general partners are limited companies (Cypriot, EU or comparable) or partnerships do the Companies Law's annual-return and accounts rules apply: the return within six months of the year-end, a late one charged €50, €1 a day for six months and €2 a day after, up to €500 (s. 64A).   160. A legal person may be director or secretary of a Cyprus company.   242. Fees for a Cyprus planning application are fixed by the Town and Country Planning (Fees) Regulations 2013 (K.D.P. 29/2013), paid on submission (reg. 3(1)). Under rule 84B of the Rules of Procedure of the Cyprus House of Representatives (published in the Gazette on 1 November 2019; parliament.cy unofficial codification of January 2020), members' bills pending before a committee at the end of a parliamentary term whose discussion has not yet begun, and members' bills tabled by MPs who were not re-elected, are deemed withdrawn at the start of the new term and struck off the committee's agenda; reviving one needs a new tabling.   309. The entry test for a Cyprus 'company of foreign interests' changed in 2022-2026. The government's Q&A (file updated 19/7/22) asked only for majority third-country ownership (or a foreign stake of at least €200,000 in nominal capital) and independent offices, applications going to the Business Facilitation Unit by e-mail or letter. A Council of Ministers decision of 30 November 2022, in force 12 December 2022, brought back the duty to prove an initial investment of at least €200,000 (Unit's page, archived 6 December 2022); an electronic system opened in December 2023; since 30 June 2026 applications go only through the company's CY Login profile, and the criterion applies 'in all the cases'.Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry / Business Support Center (gov.cy) · Strategy update action 1(γ) p. 1 and action 2(β) p. 2, archived page, 'ANNOUNCEMENT' and 'Eligibility criteria', Q&A section 2 'Business Facilitation Unit', pp. · edition: Strategy update dated 05.02.24 (Greek, 27 pages), Q&A file 'QA-update190722.pdf', web-archive snapshot 20221206233740 of · read 2026-10-05 · channel: primary · memory b330f776 · gov.cy · web.archive.org

The B-READY Methodology Handbook, Third Edition (January 2026, for the B-READY 2026 report), drops the per-step questions on business entry: experts give only total time and cost, from name verification to tax and employee registration, 'official fees only (exclude VAT)', third-party costs 'only if mandatory', overlapping steps timed by the longest. It adds five unscored questions for a foreign company: whether FDI screening is mandatory, its time, its cost including legal fees, whether a business bank account can be opened fully remotely, and how long that takes. The foreign case: USD 500,000 capital, 5 shareholders, 12 employees. So B-READY 2026 data can carry no per-step time for Cyprus.World Bank, Business Ready · Business Entry, Pillar III, General Instructions and questions 86-94, printed pp. 63-65 (PDF pp. 66-68) · edition: Methodology Handbook, Third Edition (PDF created 16 Jan 2026, modified 28 Jan 2026) · read 2026-10-06 · channel: primary · memory e08d769d · thedocs.worldbank.org

Cyprus's Advocates Law (Cap. 2, cylaw text to Law 17(I)/2024, read 6 October 2026) defines 'practising law' (s. 2(1)) as including appearing in court for anyone; preparing pleadings for a client; registering trade marks or patents; drafting, revising or amending a company's founding documents or any application, report, statement, sworn statement, resolution or other document on the formation, registration, organisation, reorganisation or dissolution of any legal person; ship registration; legal opinions; estate-administration filings. Cyprus's Advocates Law (Cap. 2, s. 11(5), cylaw text through Law 17(I)/2024, read 6 October 2026) does more than reserve the drafting of a company's memorandum and articles to a practising advocate: a practising advocate must not sign such documents that he did not draft (s. 11(5)(γ)), and any person who undertakes, holds himself out as accepting or advertises as accepting the drafting of a memorandum or articles commits an offence punishable by up to three months' imprisonment or a fine of up to £500, or both; for a legal person the same criminal liability falls on the officers who approved or voted for such acts (s. 11(5)(ε)).CyLaw (Cyprus Bar Association) - consolidated legislation · Cap. 2, s. 11(5)(α)-(ε) · edition: cylaw consolidated text, amendment history through Law 17(I)/2024 · Advocates Law, Cap. 2, s. 11(5) · read 2026-10-06 · channel: primary · memory 6e7fb745 · cylaw.org

Registrar guidance (read 6 October 2026) names no lawyer for routine changes: a change of directors or secretary (form HE4) and notice of a share transfer in a private company (HE57) are filed within 14 days, online or by hand or post, €20 each plus €20 if accelerated; late notice may cost up to €250. Changing the objects differs: the memorandum is amended by special resolution approved by the Court on an application, and filed within 15 days of the time set in the court order unless it directs otherwise (€100). In Cyprus a statutory audit may be carried out only by statutory auditors or audit firms licensed under the Auditors Law (Law 53(I)/2017, s. 33(1)); a review in place of an audit must likewise be done by a statutory auditor or audit firm (Companies Law s. 152A(1)(d)). The Auditors Law makes the Cyprus Public Audit Oversight Board (ΑΔΕΕλΕπ) the competent authority for licensing, oversight and discipline (ss. 4, 5(1), 33(2)); as of 4 Oct 2026 ICPAC states that it licenses statutory auditors under a Delegation Agreement with the Board and publishes their lists. No provision of the Cyprus Companies Law (Cap. 113) obliges a company to engage a licensed accountant for bookkeeping: s. 141(1) puts the duty to keep accounting books on the directors, and s. 141(4) accepts as a defence that a competent and reliable person was charged with it (cylaw consolidated text, read 4 Oct 2026). Licensed professionals enter elsewhere: the yearly audit or review needs a statutory auditor (s. 152A), and under s. 29 of Law 4/1978, as replaced by Law 243(I)/2025 from 1 January 2026, the tax authority may disregard accounts not prepared and certified by a statutory auditor and tax computations not prepared and certified by a holder of an ICPAC practising certificate.CyLaw (Cyprus Bar Association) - consolidated legislation · Cap. 113, s. 141(1), (4), s. 152A, word search for the stem of 'accountant' across the consolidated text, Law 4/1978 s. 29(1)-(2), Law 243(I)/2025 arts. 16, 35 · edition: cylaw consolidated text, amendments through Law 2(I)/2026 · Companies Law, Cap. 113, s. 141, Law 4/1978, s. 29, Law 243(I)/2025 · read 2026-10-04 · channel: primary · memory a4027e25 · cylaw.org · cylaw.org

The advocates' stamp is by statute a cost of the lawyer, not of the client: under s. 28 of the Cyprus Advocates Law (Cap. 2) all fees imposed under s. 27(1) are paid into the Advocates' Pension Fund, and s. 29(1) forbids an advocate to charge to or collect from any client any amount he paid as a contribution to the Fund or as fees under s. 27(1); breach is conduct incompatible with the profession and exposes him to disciplinary prosecution (s. 29(2)). Read on 4 Oct 2026 in the cylaw consolidated text, which runs to Law 17(I)/2024.   399. Cyprus lawyers have had no minimum fees for out-of-court work since 29 June 2018, when K.D.P. 172/2018 repealed the minimum-fee regulations of 1985-2017 and K.D.P. 171/2018 took effect.   402. A client unhappy with a Cyprus lawyer has two routes on the Bar's pages (read 6 October 2026). Conduct: a written complaint to the Advocates' Disciplinary Board, a statutory body chaired by the Attorney General, with a €68 fee, for fraudulent, disgraceful or unprofessional conduct or breach of the conduct rules; mishandling a case is not itself an offence. Cyprus restricts land acquisition by 'aliens' under the Immovable Property Acquisition (Aliens) Law, Cap. 109: an alien may not acquire immovable property, otherwise than on death, without the Council of Ministers' prior permission (s. 3(1)); a registration in breach is void (s. 3(5)). 'Alien' means a non-citizen and includes an alien-controlled company, a foreign company and a trust for an alien; it excludes an 'alien Cypriot' (non-citizen of Cypriot birth or descent as defined), a non-citizen wife of a citizen not separated by court decision, EU and EEA citizens, and legal persons formed under another EU state's law and seated in the EEA (s. 2).   515. Cyprus's minimum wage is reviewed on a fixed cycle. Para 7 of the Minimum Wage Decree 2022 (K.D.P. 350/2022) sets an adjustment mechanism: a nine-member committee reports to the Minister of Labour at least two months before each revision and the Minister proposes an adjustment - which may be zero - to the Council of Ministers; it applied first on 1 January 2024 and 'thereafter every two years'. The 2024 and 2026 rates followed that cycle (K.D.P. 402/2023, K.D.P. 427/2025), so the next revision falls on 1 January 2028. Paras 10-11 allow reductions: by agreement up to 15% where the employer provides food and up to 10% for accommodation; 25% for casual work of under-18s up to two months.Official Gazette of the Republic of Cyprus (cylaw copy) · K.D.P. 350/2022 paras 6, 7(1)-(2), 10, 11 · edition: K.D.P. 350/2022 as published (Gazette No. 5737, 2.9.2022), K.D.P. 402/2023, K.D.P. 427/2025 (Gazette No. 5989, 31.12.202 · K.D.P. 350/2022, paras 6-7, 10-11 · read 2026-10-05 · channel: primary · memory f6a3162a · cylaw.org · cylaw.org

Signatures and seals on documents in Cyprus are certified by certifying officers appointed by the Interior Minister under Law 165(I)/2012, at least one per municipal parish; a practising lawyer, estate agent or banker may not be one (s. 3(4)). The Law set €2 per signature or seal (s. 10(1)); the Minister's notice K.D.P. 48/2024 (Gazette No. 5856, 16 February 2024) replaced this with maximum fees per document: €5 for 1-2 pages, €10 for 3-10, €25 for 11-100, €40 above, plus at most €2 per extra signer or seal, and at most €10 for travel. No general Cyprus statute on how a power of attorney is executed was found on 6 October 2026: cylaw's index of Chapters has none, and the Contract Law (Cap. 149, Part XIII 'Agency') says only that authority may be express or implied, express when given orally or in writing (ss. 146-147). Specific acts set formalities: for a land transfer or mortgage through an agent, Law 9/1965 s. 10 requires a written authority certified by a certifying officer (or mukhtar) if signed in Cyprus, or by a Cyprus consular officer if signed abroad. Under K.D.P. 48/2024, private documents for use abroad, such as powers of attorney, go on to the Justice Ministry or citizen service centres.CyLaw (Cyprus Bar Association) - consolidated legislation and Chapter index · Cap. 149 ss. 142-148 (Part XIII 'ΑΝΤΙΠΡΟΣΩΠΕΙΑ'), cylaw Chapter index searched for 'πληρεξ', Law 9/1965 s. 10(1), (3) · edition: cylaw Cap. 149 and Chapter index as served 2026-10-06 · Contract Law, Cap. 149, ss. 146-148, Immovable Property (Transfer and Mortgage) Law 9/1965 · read 2026-10-06 · channel: primary · memory 72d2b2a3 · cylaw.org · cylaw.org

Although appearing before a court for another person is practising law reserved to licensed advocates in Cyprus (Advocates Law, Cap. 2, s. 2(1) and s. 11), s. 30 of the same Law lets every party to civil or criminal proceedings appear in person and conduct his own case; where several parties to civil proceedings share an interest, one may be authorised in writing by the others to appear for them, and the court may on a party's personal application let a close relative appear for him. CY Login's help (read 6 October 2026) lets an organisation profile add users and assistants and assign them e-services; by default its policy is that users and assistants may reach all applications. Only if the organisation switches to 'do not allow' must it name, per application, the users or assistants who may enter; if it names none, only the organisation's 'main profile', the one that created it, has access. The help publishes no list of the government e-services an organisation profile reaches; it says only that state systems will be linked to the profile 'gradually'.Department of Information Technology Services (Cyprus), CY Login · 'Διαχείριση Οργανισμού' - 'Έλεγχος Πρόσβασης Εφαρμογών', 'Γενικά' · edition: help pages as served 6 October 2026 · read 2026-10-06 · channel: primary · memory 3dc0bd2b · cge.cyprus.gov.cy · cge.cyprus.gov.cy
